event_name: 2023 Nepal Flash Flood & Landslide-Dam Breaches (Multi-Event Catalog)
watershed: Hewa Khola / Tamor Basin & Jhong Khola / Kali Gandaki

sub_events.name: Eastern Nepal Hewa Khola Flash Flood (June 17-18, 2023)
sub_events.trigger: Intense early monsoon cloudburst on steep catchment
sub_events.impact: 5 dead, 28 missing at Super Hewa Hydropower project, bridge destroyed

sub_events.name: Kagbeni Mustang Landslide-Dam Outburst Flood (August 13, 2023)
sub_events.trigger: Periglacial scree slope collapse damming Jhong Khola canyon with sudden breach
sub_events.impact: 0 deaths due to community warning, 50+ houses and Kagbeni bridge buried/damaged

sub_events.name: Western Nepal Monsoon Inundation (August 2023)
sub_events.trigger: Sustained monsoon trough causing low-gradient river drainage backwater
sub_events.impact: Urban inundation of Dhangadhi, seasonal displacement

hazard_chain: 1. Convective early-monsoon rainfall in high-gradient river valleys
2. Friable scree and colluvium slope collapse forming temporary channel chokes
3. Hydraulic barrier breach creating debris pulses
4. Severe backwater inundation and bridge destruction at settlement bottlenecks
cause_primary: Compounded Early-Monsoon Cloudbursts and Rain-Shadow Landslide Dam Outbursts (LDOF)
cause_contributing: Unconsolidated periglacial deposits in rain-shadow basins (Mustang)
Concentrated hydropower workforce camps on active alluvial terraces
Bridge structure constriction creating upstream backwater surge
data_availability_before_event: DHM automated stations operational in lower valleys; tributary stream gauges lacked real-time micro-telemetry.

key_facts.fact: Hewa Khola flash flood caused 33 casualties (5 confirmed, 28 missing) and damaged 30 hydropower projects
key_facts.source: NDRRMA Nepal Situation Report / IPPAN Report 2023

key_facts.fact: Kagbeni event demonstrated zero casualties via community early warning despite USD 7.4M structural loss
key_facts.source: District Administration Office Mustang / NDRRMA Nepal

evidence_claims.claim: Distinct regional triggers observed between Eastern monsoon flash floods and Western rain-shadow LDOFs.

lessons: Low absolute precipitation (25-40mm) in arid scree zones can trigger high-energy debris bursts
Early-monsoon flash floods frequently strike hydropower construction camps before seasonal warnings activate
Community sirens and rapid manual phone chains save lives when sensor networks are sparse

fingerprint.geology_type: Higher Himalayan Crystalline & Tethyan Sedimentary Scree
